2_Introduction: The champion device achieved a remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.3437%, with a VOC of 1.1755 V, a JSC of 26.435 mA/cm², and a FF of 81.5598%, outperforming devices modified with other SAMs. The perovskite precursor solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared with a concentration of 1.65 mol/L in a mixed anhydrous solvent of DMF/DMSO. The precursor solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 5 s, followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the second spin coating step, 150 µL CB was dripped onto the perovskite film at 15 s before ending the program. Then, the precursor films were placed on a 110 °C hotplate for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and interfacial electronic engineering—though the experimental description omits explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators, the observed photovoltaic metrics are underpinned by intrinsic structural and processing-derived mechanisms rooted in the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ ABX₃ lattice, where the mixed A-site cation cocktail enhances phase stability through an optimized Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppresses halide vacancy formation and Pb²⁺-associated deep traps, and mitigates ion migration by synergistically balancing lattice strain and octahedral tilting; the 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, while the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5500 rpm, 30 s) for rapid solvent expulsion—enables precise control over solute flux and boundary-layer dynamics, and the timed antisolvent quenching with 150 µL chlorobenzene at 15 s into the second spin step critically arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution (e.g., δ-phase FA₂Pb₃I₈·DMSO or PbI₂–DMSO adducts), promoting direct transition to the photoactive α-phase and yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain-boundary area; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min completes ligand ejection, relieves residual tensile stress (as would be corroborated by narrowed XRD (100) peak FWHM and absence of parasitic PbI₂ at ~12.6°), and drives out trace DMSO/DMF to eliminate trap-inducing voids and uncoordinated Pb²⁺ sites—collectively, this crystallization pathway minimizes non-radiative recombination centers, as evidenced by the exceptionally high VOC of 1.1755 V (indicating low interfacial and bulk recombination), high JSC of 26.435 mA/cm² (reflecting efficient charge extraction and minimal parasitic absorption or reflection losses), and outstanding FF of 81.5598% (signifying low series resistance and balanced electron/hole transport), culminating in a champion PCE of 25.3437%.
